study_guide.title: Cane and the Invisible Air

pages.text: Cane the Weather Dog sat outside when — whoosh! — his ears blew back. "Did you feel that?" said Cane. "That was the wind! But here's a puzzle… where did it come from? Let's solve it!" "First," said Cane, "a secret about air. Air is all around us, everywhere. You can't see it… but it's really there!"
pages.ask: Can you wave your hand fast in front of your face? Do you feel that little push? That's air!

pages.text: "Air is real," said Cane. "It's invisible, but you can feel it. And when air moves, we have a special name for it — wind! Wind is just moving air."

Cane wagged his tail. "Now, the big question — what makes the air move? The answer is our old friend… the Sun!" "Here's how it works," said Cane. "The Sun heats the ground. The air over the warm ground gets warm too, and warm air is light, so it rises up. Then cooler air rushes in to take its place. That rushing air is the wind!"
pages.ask: Can you make a soft whooshing wind sound?

pages.text: Just then a gentle wind rustled the leaves. "A soft, gentle wind like this is called a breeze," said Cane. "It feels nice!" Then — WHOOSH! — a sudden strong wind blew Cane's ears straight back. "Whoa! A strong, sudden burst of wind like that is called a gust!" "Weather scientists even measure the wind," said Cane. "A wind vane spins to show which way the wind blows. And a spinning cup tool called an anemometer measures how fast it goes."

The wind grew stronger, and the big trees began to sway. Cane's ears perked up. "When the wind gets really strong, we stay away from big trees and power lines, and we head inside. Strong wind means be weather-smart!" Soon the gust passed, and only a gentle breeze was left. Cane lifted his nose into it and smiled. "Air is invisible — but I can always feel the wind. And now, so can you!" "Great job, weather watcher," said Cane. "You solved the puzzle of the wind. You are weather-ready!"

study_guide.rule: Wind is moving air — and the Sun's heat is what makes it move.
